reference_disclaimer: This is a screenshot of the implemented, composed application, not a drawn mockup. It was generated by the registered network-isolated application_diff_workbench_public_path CTest course at implementation commit 6e07773b084b80a2079ea6f123b252d5c221126b. The course uses the tests-enabled GitHub.com contract fixture under offscreen QFusionStyle at device-pixel ratio 1.0; no live or private GitHub content is present. The selected current right-side thread is anchored to review.cpp line 42. The ordinary selected-line band and the narrow blue left-margin marker are visible in the right pane, while the root and reply remain in the conversation drawer. Three things changed since the batch the owner rejected, all of them their own direction: the source panes now show line numbers (BPR-0455), replies read as a linear feed grouped by root rather than a per-depth staircase (BPR-0456), and the files drawer is collapsed so more source is visible. The conversations drawer also carries BPR-0418's thread map above the thread; that surface is not what this question asks about, and its own iteration is tracked on BPR-0211. Production places this RIGHT anchor only after exact accepted-head identity agrees. Production LEFT placement fails closed because merge-base identity is unavailable; endpoint-agnostic Qt tests cover the future exact-left widget contract, not current production behavior. Any missing or unknown side and any current LINE root missing its current Line are rejected by the provider; an outdated LINE root may carry only OriginalLine, and replies inherit the root. Defensive widget tests cover synthetic invalid projections. Accept authorizes this marker-and-drawer boundary. Reject means the comment body should enter the code view and requires an RFC amendment or successor scope; it does not authorize that change by itself.

acceptance_criteria: The selected drawer thread is unmistakably associated with right-side line 42
The root and reply remain readable without inserting prose into the source document
The narrow margin marker plus ordinary selected-line band is enough confirmation after navigation
Keeping natural source layout uninterrupted is the right tradeoff for the shipped drawer

audit_verdict.note: The registered network-isolated composed public-path course asserts the selected root, exact right-side zero-based line 41, one remaining drawer root, a non-empty margin-marker rectangle, and the saved render. Provider contracts reject a missing side and a current LINE root missing its current Line, while permitting an outdated LINE root to carry only OriginalLine and carrying the validated response head identity. The composed production course binds current RIGHT placement to that exact accepted-head identity. Focused endpoint-agnostic Qt tests cover right placement, reverse filtering, future exact-left caller behavior, and defensive non-placement. Human product direction remains required only for whether the body should cross into the code view.

subjects.description: BPR-0414 implements exact drawer-to-code navigation and exact code-line-to-drawer filtering. In the production GitHub path, a current right-side root is placeable only after the response head identity matches the accepted head; unsafe, outdated, file-level, or incomplete anchors remain unplaced rather than guessed. Selecting this drawer thread reveals right-side line 42 through the existing semantic line-selection path. The remaining choice is where the prose belongs. Accept means the code view stays a natural source document with the narrow marker and selected-line band as its conversation indication while the root and replies remain readable in the drawer. Reject means that boundary is insufficient and the comment body should be designed into the code view, which conflicts with RFC-BPR-0005's current no-inline-row rule and therefore needs explicit successor scope.

items.definition: Exactly one current thread remains after file, right-side, and line-42 filtering; its reply stays beneath the root.
The right pane reveals source line 42, paints its ordinary selected-line band, and adds a 4 px marker at the pane's left margin.
Both panes remain the natural source documents. No comment body, synthetic alignment blank, or full-width inline conversation row is inserted.

detail_sections.heading: What unattended verification already decides
items: GitHub DiffSide RIGHT and the current Line are fetched separately from OriginalLine; any missing/unknown side and any current LINE root missing its current Line fail the provider contract, while an outdated LINE root may carry only OriginalLine.
A reply inherits its root thread's exact path, side, current/original line, and placement availability.
The production GitHub course places the pictured current RIGHT root only when headRefOid matches the accepted head exactly.
Production LEFT placement fails closed because the response lacks the merge-base identity required to match GitHub's left coordinate to the accepted base-tip pane.
A source-line gesture filters to exact file plus side plus line; changing back to a group/file selection restores file-level thread scope.
Outdated, file-level, unsafe, and synthetic invalid projections never receive a guessed marker.

known_concerns: The 4 px margin marker is intentionally restrained and may be too subtle without the selected-line band
A wide conversations drawer reduces the comparison width, especially on compact windows
The screenshot uses a synthetic fixture thread and offscreen QFusionStyle rather than live content and target-native styling
Production currently fails closed for LEFT anchors because the provider cannot prove the GitHub merge-base coordinate matches the accepted base-tip pane
Outdated, file-level, and otherwise unsafe anchors remain visibly in the drawer with a reason but receive no guessed code marker; those states are covered by tests, not this image

This is the second time this question has been asked. Batch 0a6b4763976a05a7f14af6df was rejected on 2026-08-25 because no line number was visible anywhere, so the criterion about line 42 could not be judged, and because replies were indented per depth. Both are fixed and the files drawer is now collapsed as asked. The question itself is unchanged and remains unanswered: rejecting it does not authorise comment bodies in the code view, and accepting it does not endorse the line-number or reply-feed work, which have their own evidence.
